newsitem.title: USA: CME TO BEGIN TRADING E-MINI S&P 500 SEPTEMBER 9.
newsitem.headline: CME TO BEGIN TRADING E-MINI S&P 500 SEPTEMBER 9.

text.p: Trading in mini Standard and Poor's 500 futures and options contracts on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange will begin September 9, the exchange said Tuesday.
The contracts will be traded primarily electronically.

The so-called e-mini S&P 500 futures will be priced at $50 times the S&P 500 index, or about $48,000 at recent trading levels. The e-mini contracts, sized at one-tenth the current size of the CME's flagship S&P 500 futures contract, are expected to attract investors for whom the the current S&P 500 index is too large, the CME said.
The CME said the contracts will be executed on its GLOBEX electronic trading system, with orders routed through various means including, as a final phase, the Internet.

Orders for options and for fewer than 30 futures contracts will use completely electronic order entry, while larger orders will be executed by open outcry on the trading floor via all-or-none trading.
The CME said "virtual" or simulated e-mini trading will be available through its website at www.cme.com ahead of the launch through an arrangement with Audiotrack Inc.
The simulated trade is based on a program that incorporates liquidity and other characteristics of similar contracts that are already trading, as well as the e-mini's particular specifications.
After the September 9 e-mini launch, the virtual trading will incorporate actual market conditions and prices. Virtual traders will be allotted $100,000 in simulated funds to trade.
The CME said Audiotrack's usual transaction fees have been waived, and users will pay a $10 processing fee to simulate trading CME products on line for one month.
